population: production TuringLLM 8k, held-out strongest, non-vacuous (merge.py v2)

members.label: Music theory terms
members.description: Fires on tokens within music-theory words (major, chord progressions, tonality, tonal) in Western music contexts; predicts music-related next tokens like 'musical', 'music', 'melody'.

members.label: Music-context noun, predicts music
members.description: Fires on nouns ending music-related phrases (harmony, structures, expressions) in music-theory text, and promotes music-related next tokens like "musical", "Music", "music".

members.label: Network/system word pieces (unclear)
members.description: Fires on mixed word-fragment tokens (' organ', 'connected', ' Boolean', ' cent') in network/city/system contexts; weak consistency. Logits mildly favor ' networks', ' nodes', ' relationships'.

rows.label: Social/political theme words in music-society text
rows.description: Fires on abstract social-topic nouns or adjectives (' political', ' change', ' interaction(s)', ' ideas') in lists of social/cultural themes, especially in text about music as a vehicle for social change. Silent on 'political' in other generic social-systems contexts.

members.label: Token ' essentially' (unclear output)
members.description: Fires only on the token ' essentially' (6 of 6 peaks). The evidence is thin, and the logit effects are mixed with no clear next-token pattern, though ' essentially' itself is boosted.

members.label: Document-start token (unclear)
members.description: Fires only on the document-start <s> token (6 of 6 peaks, one example window). Logit effects are mixed and don't show a clear next-token pattern, so the function is unclear.

members.label: ' simply' token
members.description: Fires on the token ' simply' (all 6 peaks, e.g. "simply means that instead…"). Logits boost ' simply' itself and are otherwise mixed, so the output effect is unclear.

rows.label: Essentially/simply/merely adverbs
rows.description: Fires on hedging/minimizing adverbs such as " essentially", " simply", " merely" and " literally", mostly directly before a verb or predicate (means, represent, serves as). Members are mainly detectors of these adverb tokens.

members.label: Biochemistry term fragments
members.description: Fires on word fragments inside cell-biology/biochemistry terms (bisph-osph-ate, Kre-bs, cell-ular); promotes cell/biology next tokens like cells, memb, bio, protein. Few examples, so somewhat tentative.

members.label: " chrom" word-start fragment
members.description: Fires only on the word-fragment token " chrom" (start of chromatography, chromatid, chromosome, chromatin), and it predicts continuations like "atin", "omer", "atch".

members.label: "fect" in "Perfect" tense
members.description: Fires on the token "fect" in "Perfect" within grammar headings like "Future/Past/Conditional Perfect Continuous". Predicts little clearly; weak push toward "-", "(", "is".

rows.label: Biochemistry word pieces (chrom, omer, II)
rows.description: Fires on word pieces in biology/chemistry science terms, mainly ' chrom' (chromosome/chromatography), 'omer' in Isomerase/Isomerism, ' II' in meiosis phases, and ' pol' (poles). Needs a technical science context; silent on abstract physics text.

members.label: replaced [by/with]
members.description: Fires on 'by' or 'with' right after a form of "replaced" (replaced by/with). Logits mildly favor words like 'newer'/'new' as the replacement, but the evidence is thin (6 examples).

members.label: Replacement words (replacing/with/of)
members.description: Fires on replacement-related tokens, mainly " replacing", also " with" after "replaced" and " of" after "replacement". Predicts the thing replaced, such as " old", " original" or " existing".

members.label: Mixed function words, unclear
members.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' at', ' with', ' lif', ' model') mostly after passive verbs or mid-phrase in technical/business prose; peaks are inconsistent and logits are unclear.

rows.label: 'by' after 'replaced'
rows.description: Fires on ' by' right after "replaced" (passive replacement, e.g. "traditional methods were replaced by"), and weakly on the following word. Silent on ' by' after other verbs like "driven by" or "monitored by".

members.label: " ret" word-start token
members.description: Fires on the token " ret" as the start of "retention", mostly in chromatography "retention times" contexts. Predicts word completions like "ail", "ina", "irement", though the logits are mixed.

members.label: " ret" word-start token
members.description: Fires on the split token " ret" at the start of a word, mostly "retention" (also "retail"). It predicts the continuation "ention" and similar suffixes.

members.label: ret/curr word-fragment tokens
members.description: Fires on word-start fragments " ret" (in "online retail/retailers") and " curr" (in "currencies/currents"), i.e. a split-word first piece. Logits are mixed, so the next-token prediction is unclear.

rows.label: Word-start piece " ret"
rows.description: Fires on the word-start piece " ret" (retailer, retail, retention, retina), where more letters must follow. Members are detectors of " ret" plus related word-start pieces. Weak activity on "qui" and "df".

members.label: Digit 4 in year (14xx)
members.description: Fires on the token '4' as the second digit of a four-digit year in the 1400s (e.g., "1[[4]]43"). Only one example is shown, and the logit effects look unclear.

members.label: Digit 4 in 14xx years
members.description: Fires on the digit "4" as the second digit of a 15th-century-style year (e.g., 1[4]43, 1[4]75) in historical dates. Logit effects are unclear and mixed.

members.label: Digit 2 inside numbers
members.description: Fires on the digit "2" when it is the second digit inside a multi-digit number (e.g. 12, 1[2]00, 1[2]25) in numeric lists or codes. Logits are mixed and unclear.

rows.label: '4' in 14xx years
rows.description: Fires on the digit '4' as the third digit of a year in the 1400s, such as 1443, 1449 or 1475. It stays silent on '4' in other year positions or other digit contexts.

members.label: Predicts patterns/behavior continuation
members.description: Fires on connective or verb tokens (' and', ' that', ' understand') after words like habits, patterns, or behavior, in analytics or science text. It predicts 'patterns', 'behavior' and 'predict' next.

members.label: List continuation in course descriptions (unclear)
members.description: Fires on commas, "and", and word endings like "ics" inside lists of topics or activities in academic/course-style descriptions. Mixed peaks and weak logits, so unclear.

members.label: Mid-word subword tokens in all-caps text
members.description: Fires on fragment tokens (VE, ED, H, U) inside words in ALL-CAPS text, often near document start. Peaks are mixed and logits are unclear, so the label is tentative.

rows.label: Academic science text, mixed function-word positions
rows.description: Fires on varied tokens (' patterns', ' the', ' to', verbs like 'understand') in academic descriptions of scientific fields (geography, epidemiology, climate, energy). It is silent on ' patterns' in some climate contexts, so the evidence is mixed and the condition is unclear.

members.label: " sequ" word-start fragment
members.description: Fires on the word-fragment token " sequ" (start of "sequential", "sequencing"), and predicts completions like "ential", "enced", "entially".

members.label: sequ token fragment (sequencing)
members.description: Fires only on the word-fragment " sequ", mostly in "sequencing" contexts (genomics). It predicts suffix completions like "ential", "entially", "enced", "encing", "enc".

members.label: ' Tra' token (Traffic), unclear
members.description: Fires on the word-start token ' Tra' (as in "Traffic") at the start of a document or sentence. The logits push suffixes like "-entially" and "-ential", which don't fit "Traffic", so the evidence is thin and unclear.

rows.label: ' sequ' word-start piece
rows.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' sequ' (sequential, sequencing, sequenced), predicting continuations like 'ential', 'enced', 'encing'. Members are mostly ' sequ' detectors, plus a few other word-start pieces.

members.label: " random" in randomization techniques
members.description: Fires only on the token " random" in statistical or ML contexts, such as random subspaces, block randomization and stratified random sampling. It often comes before a suffix or noun like -ness, generator, Forest or injection.

members.label: "random" before randomization suffixes
members.description: Fires only on the token " random" in statistics/ML/experimental-design contexts. It predicts word-completion suffixes like "ized", "ization", "ising" and "sampling", and suppresses unrelated tokens.

members.label: ' random' token (statistics)
members.description: Fires only on the token " random" in statistics and experimental-design contexts (random sampling, randomization). It predicts suffixes such as "ization", "ized", "walk" and "isation".

rows.label: ' random' / ' randomly' token
rows.description: Fires on the word "random" or "randomly" (also randomization pieces), mostly in statistics and sampling text such as random sampling, random assignment, random forest. It pushes toward words like sampling, generator, assignment.
